Update (Sept 18): following 1,400+ public comments, the board substantially revised the proposal -- cutting maximum leave from 18 to 12 weeks, exempting employers with fewer than 15 employees, and raising the eligibility threshold from 30 days to 180 days/625 hours worked. The board did not vote this week as expected; the recommendation vote is now set for a special meeting Sept 28 at noon.
stories.score_note: Live, in-progress change to what would have been one of the most generous local paid-leave mandates in the country.

stories.headline: PA Supreme Court removes spoiler candidate from PA-07 ballot
stories.one_line: The state Supreme Court affirmed the Commonwealth Court ruling that Andrew Tupone -- a former registered Republican who filed as a Green Party candidate without the party's knowledge -- cannot appear on the PA-07 November ballot. Sets a two-way race: Republican incumbent Ryan Mackenzie vs. Democrat Bob Brooks.
stories.score_note: A court ruling that directly sets the ballot for a competitive US House race.

stories.headline: Trump says he faces a 'big decision' on whether to 'annihilate' Iran's regime
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple for the remark itself; Single-reliable-source for the AP targeting-error detail
stories.one_line: In a Thursday Axios interview, Trump: 'I have a big decision coming up. Do I want to go in and annihilate them or do I not?' Officials cited say a Gulf-leaders meeting around next week's UNGA is a likely moment of clarity. Sits in direct tension with his own claim of 'direct' contact with Iran and hope the war is 'nearing the end' -- Iran's SNSC secretary Rezaei rejected that framing as 'mixed signals.' Backdrop: Tuesday's UN war-crimes report (White House called it 'unserious nonsense' Thursday; Pentagon's own Minab probe 'remains ongoing,' with one unnamed AP official citing outdated DIA targeting data, unconfirmed). Update (Sept 18 pm): South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said at a Friday press conference South Korea 'will not' send troops for the Iran war or to the Strait of Hormuz, the clearest on-record response yet to Trump's repeated requests, leaving open only a narrower role protecting South Korea's own shipping. Separately, UKMTO reported a second Hormuz tanker incident Friday and Iran's IRGC claimed it struck and detained a Togo-flagged tanker (Trend) for an alleged unauthorized passage; neither the vessel identity nor the claim of authorship is independently confirmed. Saturday's Weekly Review carries this as the lead story of the week, tying it to Tuesday's scheduled Gulf-leaders meeting at the UN General Assembly as the next forcing event.
stories.score_note: A genuine, unresolved contradiction in the administration's own public Iran-war messaging within the same week.

stories.headline: G7 demands Houthi halt as Yemen war widens and a second unclaimed tanker is hit near Hormuz
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple for the G7 statement and Riyadh/Aramco strike; Single-reliable-source for the Kahboub Mountains push and the Muscat stand-down channel
stories.one_line: G7 nations (Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, UK, US) issued a joint statement today demanding the Houthis cease all military action and end attacks on shipping, and calling on Iran to end its support. Follows Saturday's Houthi ballistic-missile attempt on Riyadh (intercepted, debris ignited an Aramco fuel-depot fire) and a claimed Yanbu Aramco strike, plus a Yemeni civilian killed by intercepted-drone debris. Five Yemeni military sources (Reuters, single chain) say the Houthis are pushing to seize the Kahboub Mountains in Taiz/Lahij. Trump reportedly called off planned US strikes at the last minute after MbS pressure, with a Muscat, Oman channel reportedly securing a Houthi commitment not to target US vessels (still single-sourced, unconfirmed by a second chain). Separately, an unclaimed strike hit a tanker approaching Hormuz Sept 21 (UKMTO), the second such unattributed incident this month; Trump and Macron pledged in New York to 'act together' on energy-infrastructure protection and Hormuz freedom of navigation, without a concrete plan.
stories.score_note: A G7 diplomatic intervention into an escalating war most Americans don't know is happening, days before Trump hosts Xi and while US-Iran hostilities remain unresolved.

stories.headline: Massie and Khanna say they have 218 signatures for a second Epstein files discharge petition
stories.one_line: Reps. Massie (R-KY) and Khanna (D-CA) announced Thursday they have commitments for all 218 signatures needed to force a floor vote on the 'Epstein Files Transparency Act II,' giving state AGs, victims and members of Congress standing to sue DOJ over noncompliance with the original Transparency Act. Four Republicans committed (Massie, Norman, Mace, Fitzpatrick) plus every Democrat. Second successful discharge petition by the same pair; the original passed the House 427-1 in Nov 2025. No vote possible until the House returns from its post-midterms recess. Update (Sept 21): the claimed 218 signatures cannot be formally filed/certified until the House returns from its recess, which runs until after the midterms -- a procedural detail tempering the 'signatures secured' framing without changing the count.
stories.score_note: A rare bipartisan supermajority discharge effort, twice now, on the same subject.
sources: Reps. Massie's and Khanna's own statements (primary)

stories.headline: Early voting for the 2026 midterms opens in Virginia, South Dakota and Minnesota
stories.one_line: Friday, Sept 18 marks the start of ballot mailing/in-person absentee voting in VA, SD and MN, the first states to open voting for the Nov 3 midterms. In Minnesota, the full state legislature, all statewide offices, every US House seat and one US Senate seat are on the ballot; full in-person early voting there opens Oct 16.
stories.score_note: Practical start of the midterm election cycle nationally.

stories.headline: Internal DHS document raises questions about a noncitizen-voting effort tied to the midterms
stories.verification: Single-reliable-source (NPR's own original reporting); DHS's on-record denial included
stories.one_line: NPR reports it obtained an internal DHS email (dated last December, released via a DNC public-records lawsuit) in which a DHS border-policy official sent a 78-page list of counties/states offering non-English election materials to Rob Law (DHS Undersecretary) and Heather Honey (leads the administration's noncitizen-voting effort), with a DOJ voter-prosecution 'criminal checklist' attached. Democrats quoted by NPR fear the pairing could intimidate voters in non-English-speaking communities. DHS told NPR on the record it 'is not planning operations targeting polling locations.' No concrete enforcement action reported tied to the list.
stories.score_note: Single-newsroom original reporting; DHS denial given equal prominence pending independent corroboration.

stories.headline: Poland's Tusk warns Russia may stage 'accidental' hybrid strikes on NATO allies
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple for the warning itself; the underlying Russian-intent claim is Single-reliable-source/System inference (Polish government characterization)
stories.one_line: PM Tusk told parliament Thursday Russia is planning drone/rocket strikes on Poland and other NATO members supporting Ukraine, to be presented as 'accidental' to test Article 5 resolve; Russia's foreign ministry called it 'contrived.' Separately, Trump said 'major progress' is being made toward a permanent US Army base in Poland (sites near Powidz/Poznan visited by a Pentagon delegation), even as the Pentagon separately weighs broader European troop cuts. Update (Sept 18 pm): Polish Deputy Defense Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka said any potential US Army base under discussion would 'definitely' be sited in western Poland -- the first concrete detail beyond Trump's Thursday 'great progress' post; no site, troop count or finalized agreement announced.
stories.score_note: A NATO ally's head of government publicly warning of staged 'accidental' attacks is a notable escalation in alliance messaging.

stories.headline: Chrome and Microsoft zero-days need patching today, alongside Saturday's Cisco ISE deadline
stories.one_line: Chrome's sixth 2026 zero-day, CVE-2026-85046 (CVSS 8.8, V8 sandbox escape), has a CISA federal patch deadline today. Microsoft's September Patch Tuesday fixed ~966-974 CVEs (largest on record) including two already-exploited zero-days now in CISA's KEV catalog: CVE-2026-81963 (Windows Update Stack's first-ever exploited zero-day) and CVE-2026-85880 (Windows ALPC heap overflow). Lands within 48 hours of the already-tracked maximum-severity Cisco ISE flaw (CVE-2026-76460), whose federal deadline is tomorrow.
stories.score_note: Three maximum-attention vulnerabilities across three vendors with federal deadlines within 48 hours of each other.

stories.headline: King Charles hosts an AI safety summit; Palantir's Karp calls for nationalizing AI labs
stories.one_line: Palantir CEO Alex Karp told CNBC Thursday leading AI labs may need to be nationalized, with developers facing civil/criminal liability, suggesting some labs might welcome nationalization to dodge client-data lawsuits. Same day, King Charles III convened a closed-door AI safety summit at Dumfries House, Scotland (~30 attendees incl. OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Google DeepMind, UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan, a Vatican AI adviser), warning of 'existential dangers' if AI fell 'into the wrong hands'; no binding agreement resulted. Lands amid the Amodei 'pace the frontier' vs. Zuckerberg self-regulation split already tracked; none of the five (or seven, per some outlets -- discrepancy unresolved) China-based firms Anthropic accused of distilling Claude has responded, nor has Anthropic responded to Suleyman's 'constitution' critique.
stories.score_note: Within one week, a head of state, a major AI-infra CEO and two top labs have all publicly signaled real anxiety about frontier AI's trajectory with no consensus on the remedy.

stories.headline: Karman Holdings names a new CFO; shares fall despite bullish analyst coverage
stories.one_line: Karman named Chris Boynton CFO effective Sept 14, succeeding Mike Willis (departs by year-end after a transition). A Sept 16 investor presentation touted >25% organic growth (2025/2026e), ~1.6x book-to-bill (trailing 18 months) and ~30% adjusted EBITDA margin; Guggenheim initiated at Buy, $63 target. Shares nonetheless fell 4.57% Thursday, the lone decliner in an otherwise strong space-sector session -- no confirmed catalyst identified for the divergence. Update (Sept 21): the Sept 16 8-K flagged pending exhibit review is a routine Item 7.01 Reg FD disclosure furnishing an investor presentation signed by CEO Jon Rambeau -- no material corporate action. Resolved, no longer watched.
stories.score_note: Leadership change plus a share-price divergence from bullish coverage worth tracking.

stories.headline: PRT plans to buy 102 new buses for $94.1 million amid federal funding squeeze
stories.one_line: Pittsburgh Regional Transit announced a plan to buy 102 New Flyer buses (6 electric, 96 diesel) for $94.1M, pending full board approval Sept 25; if approved, buses enter service next summer. Comes against the backdrop of PRT's already-tracked $7.3M federal continuing-resolution funding cut.
stories.score_note: Fleet investment decision amid an ongoing federal funding squeeze, relevant to South Hills riders.

stories.headline: Judge Kelly to hear CNN/MS NOW/Politico's press-ban TRO request at 3:30 PM today
stories.one_line: Suit filed Monday morning in US District Court for DC (First Amendment/due-process claims; Trump, Cheung, Curran, Wiles named) was assigned to Judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee who ruled for CNN's Jim Acosta on due-process grounds in 2018. Kelly ordered the administration's TRO response by today, Sept 22; a hearing has been widely reported for Wednesday afternoon but is not yet docket-confirmed. ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC suspended TV press-pool coverage in apparent solidarity. The White House responded with a 'privilege, not a right' statement citing Obama/Biden-era precedent, and separately launched a 24/7 'Trump TV' YouTube stream Monday. Update (Sept 22 pm): the Wednesday-afternoon hearing before Judge Kelly, reported this morning as not yet docket-confirmed, is now confirmed. No ruling issued. Update (Sept 23 am): DOJ's late-Tuesday filing argues press access is 'a privilege, not a right' revocable 'at the president's will,' citing national-security concerns tied to Iran-war and ballroom-construction coverage. Hearing set for 3:30 PM today; Trump himself predicted on Truth Social that Kelly will rule against him given the Acosta precedent and that he'll have to appeal.
stories.score_note: A press-freedom lawsuit with a Trump-appointed judge who has already ruled against the administration on nearly identical facts once before.

stories.headline: Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway's chairman after six decades
stories.one_line: Berkshire Hathaway announced Friday that Warren Buffett, 96, is stepping down as chairman effective immediately, becoming chairman emeritus; his son Howard Buffett, a Berkshire director for 33 years, becomes chairman. Buffett had already handed the CEO role to Greg Abel in 2025; in his shareholder letter he wrote 'Father Time always wins' and said Abel had 'exceeded' his expectations. Berkshire's Class B shares fell roughly 1% on the news; the stock is up only about 1% year-to-date against the S&P 500's 11%-plus gain.
stories.score_note: Closes a 60-year chapter at one of the most closely watched companies in American finance.

stories.headline: Fed's Bowman: the central bank's own supervisors missed the warning signs before SVB's collapse
stories.one_line: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman, speaking in London Friday, unveiled an independent review (Starling Advisory Group) finding Fed supervisory staff 'knew, or should have known' about Silicon Valley Bank's vulnerabilities as early as March 2022 but failed to act promptly, citing a 'long-standing culture of risk aversion.' The review found Trump-era regulatory tailoring played no role in the failure, clearing former Vice Chair Randal Quarles. Bowman separately said a revamped, less 'opaque' bank stress-testing framework will be finalized 'in the coming weeks.' Carried as a Top Story in today's edition for fuller context (stress-test reform specifics); no new facts beyond the original Sept 18 speech -- Board expected to consider final revisions 'in the coming weeks.'
stories.score_note: A sitting Fed vice chair publicly faulting her own agency's supervisors, not deregulation, for a bank failure, while previewing a looser stress-test regime.
sources: Fed Vice Chair Bowman's speech texts (primary, federalreserve.gov)

stories.headline: Russia opens a three-day election amid fears of a post-vote mobilization wave
stories.verification: Confirmed-primary (election itself); Disputed/Single-source (the 300,000-conscript figure, from one unnamed European official; Putin explicitly denies any mobilization plan)
stories.one_line: Russia's State Duma election runs Sept 18-20. Bloomberg and other outlets report growing fear inside Russia of a mass mobilization once the vote ends; one unnamed European security official cited a figure of up to 300,000 additional conscripts by year-end. Putin called the warnings 'complete nonsense'; Zelensky said he expects any call-up in late September or early October. Same day, Russia struck Zaporizhzhia with roughly 93 drones, destroying a shopping complex, and hit a Kherson hospital's grounds with a drone-dropped explosive (no casualties reported there). Update (weekend): voting concluded Sunday with turnout at 44.75% as of 6am Moscow time, below 2021's final 51.7%; exit polls put United Russia at 53.5%, CPRF 14.5%, LDPR 10.1% -- an easy retention of the party's existing supermajority, not in doubt. Independent monitors reported ballot-stuffing allegations at roughly 4,500 polling stations, unaddressed by the government. Separately Friday, Trump signed the bipartisan 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' (86-11 Senate, 262-159 House) targeting Russia's energy/defense sectors and shadow fleet, with an unusually critical signing statement calling parts of his own bill 'significantly flawed.'
stories.score_note: A specific, dated political trigger (the election's close) for a potential major escalation in Russian force generation, with the underlying figure explicitly disputed by the Kremlin.

stories.headline: Voting-rights coalition sues over armed federal agents at polling places as early voting opens
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (lawsuit itself); Single-reliable-source (NPR's second DHS-document report)
stories.one_line: A nine-organization coalition led by the NAACP (with AALDEF litigating) filed suit Friday in U.S. District Court for D.C., arguing administration suggestions that armed ICE officers could appear near polling sites amount to illegal voter intimidation under the Voting Rights Act. Separately, NPR reports obtaining an internal DHS email (dated last December) pairing a 78-page list of non-English-language voting jurisdictions with a DOJ prosecution 'checklist,' sent to officials leading the administration's noncitizen-voting review; DHS told NPR on the record it 'is not planning operations targeting polling locations.' Both land the day early voting opened in Virginia, South Dakota and Minnesota.
stories.score_note: Two distinct legal/reporting threads converging on the same question -- federal enforcement activity chilling turnout -- arriving as voting itself begins.

stories.headline: US growth data cools: industrial output stalls, first manufacturing decline in seven months
stories.one_line: August industrial production was flat (0.0%, missing a ~+0.2-0.3% consensus); manufacturing output fell 0.3%, its first decline after seven straight gains, though computer/electronic-products and electrical-equipment utilization both rose, consistent with continued AI-infrastructure capex. Capacity utilization held at 76.3%. Separately, the Conference Board's Leading Economic Index fell 0.1% to 99.5, its first decline since March; the Board still projects 1.9% 2026 GDP growth but trimmed 2027 to 1.8%.
stories.score_note: Two independent gauges turning down the same day is a modest but genuine cooling signal, two days after the Fed's hawkish hike.

stories.headline: Sudan gold-mine collapse kills dozens in RSF-held territory
stories.one_line: The Sudanese Doctors Network reported at least 67 dead in a gold-mine collapse at Al-Zaraa, West Kordofan (RSF-controlled); an anonymous RSF source cited by AFP put the toll at least 82. Neither figure independently verifiable given the absence of independent access to the area, itself a consequence of Sudan's ongoing civil war, now in its fourth year amid famine conditions the WFP says affect 24.6 million people.
stories.score_note: A major casualty event in an active conflict zone with no independent access to verify either attributed toll.
sources: anonymous RSF source via AFP (primary, single-source, disputed)

stories.headline: White House withdraws ICE director nominee amid Rand Paul hold
stories.one_line: The White House withdrew Lance Schroyer's nomination to lead Immigration and Customs Enforcement on Thursday, after Sen. Rand Paul held up the nomination in committee over questions about a Minnesota agent-involved shooting. No successor nominee named. This report did not cover the withdrawal in Thursday's or Friday morning's edition despite same-day coverage; disclosed as a coverage gap, logged to the corrections ledger.
stories.score_note: A stalled Cabinet-adjacent nomination tied to an unresolved use-of-force question, disclosed here as a coverage gap.

stories.headline: PennDOT adds nighttime I-79 lane restrictions to an already-busy fall of South Fayette road work
stories.one_line: PennDOT will begin nighttime joint-and-crack sealing on I-79 in South Fayette Township starting Friday, Sept 26, 7 PM-6 AM lane restrictions between the PA Turnpike/PIT/Morganza Rd interchange and the Route 50/Bridgeville exit, through early November -- layering onto the already-underway Route 50 signal-upgrade project through late November. Update (Sept 22): board vote on the $94.1M/102-bus order (56 60ft diesel, 6 60ft electric, 40 35ft diesel) is set for this Friday, Sept 25.
stories.score_note: New road-work announcement directly affecting Bridgeville-area commutes.

stories.headline: PA PUC votes to rewrite emergency electric load-control rules as data centers strain the grid
stories.one_line: Pennsylvania's Public Utility Commission voted 5-0 to direct staff to draft updated regulations on when/how customers can be curtailed during grid emergencies, citing PJM's projected 6,831-MW reliability shortfall for 2028-29 tied partly to data-center demand. A technical conference on cost allocation is planned this fall; a tentative plan is due at the PUC's Oct 1 meeting.
stories.score_note: State-level regulatory response to data-center driven grid strain, relevant to Logan's home state.

stories.headline: Houthi missiles reach Riyadh for the first time; Trump cuts short Camp David, weighs strikes in Yemen
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (the Riyadh/Yanbu strike); Single-reliable-source-cluster, developing (Sunday's Saudi retaliation on Sanaa)
stories.one_line: Houthi forces fired missiles and drones at Riyadh and Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu before dawn Saturday -- the first strike on the Saudi capital since the war widened, intercepted by Saudi air defenses with no reported casualties. Trump cut short a planned Camp David weekend and returned to the White House as the administration weighed direct strikes in Yemen, per reporting this outlet could not fully independently corroborate; the State Department expanded Middle East travel guidance, warning of rapid escalation potential. Saudi Arabia struck back at Sanaa early Sunday, reported by a regional wire and secondary trackers rather than a major international wire; casualty specifics remain unconfirmed. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has now asked Trump twice for direct US strikes on the Houthis, both declined in favor of intelligence support only. Update (Sept 21): Houthi forces are pushing to seize the Kahboub Mountains highlands (Taiz/Lahij) -- the last high ground separating their Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed government territory -- per five Yemeni military sources (Reuters); Saudi Arabia has launched hundreds of strikes there as government forces reportedly withdraw. UN: ~700 killed, 120,000+ displaced in this flare-up. Separately, UKMTO reports an unidentified projectile struck a tanker entering the Strait of Hormuz today, lightly injuring 2 crew; no claim of responsibility. Fuller reporting on Sunday's called-off US strikes says munitions were being loaded before Trump aborted at the last minute citing a direct US-Houthi channel -- Reuters could not independently verify, CENTCOM has not commented.
stories.score_note: First direct strike on the Saudi capital itself, raising the political cost of continued US restraint the same week Trump described facing a 'big decision' on Iran.
sources: Houthi and Saudi coalition statements (primary, disputed)

stories.headline: Woodland Hills school board votes to terminate superintendent Joe Maluchnik's contract
stories.one_line: The Woodland Hills school board voted Friday to formally terminate Superintendent Joe Maluchnik's contract following reported friction over the district's direction. Not previously reported by this outlet; disclosed here roughly two days after the fact rather than folded in as newly broken.
stories.score_note: Allegheny County school-district leadership change, disclosed with the coverage gap acknowledged.
sources: Woodland Hills school board (primary, meeting action)

stories.headline: Trump prepares to host Xi Wed-Thu as China calls the $14B Taiwan arms package a possible dealbreaker
stories.one_line: Xi's visit runs Wednesday-Thursday with a Thursday state dinner. China's foreign ministry reiterated the Taiwan arms package could derail the summit and separately dismissed Trump's new Russia/Iran sanctions law as 'illicit.' Bessent proposed a US-China AI incident-notification channel in Sunday talks with Vice Premier He Lifeng; Beijing's own readout mentioned AI only briefly. One single-sourced SCMP report says Trump may delay signing the Taiwan package until December as leverage.
stories.score_note: A first White House visit in a decade for Xi, opening under an explicit Chinese threat to disrupt it.
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple on summit dates/agenda; Single-reliable-source on December-delay speculation

stories.headline: Russia's Duma election finalizes with a record United Russia majority amid fraud and hacking claims
stories.one_line: With ~95% counted, United Russia holds 57.83-57.86% of the party-list vote, projected ~355/450 seats (record, above 343 in 2016); official results due Oct 5. Novaya Gazeta Europe (via Meduza) estimates the unmanipulated result would be ~34%. Anonymous group 'CikLeak' claims to have breached CEC/'Vybory 2.0' contractor infrastructure days before the vote. Nearly 1,300 KPRF/Yabloko observers reportedly barred from polling stations in various regions. CEC has not responded to either claim.
stories.score_note: First wartime Duma election, with the first hard fraud/hacking allegations surfacing since polls closed.
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple on vote tally; Single-reliable-source (Meduza chain) on fraud-scale estimate and hacking claim

stories.headline: Record Moscow drone barrage draws a deadly Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia
stories.one_line: Zelensky says Russian drones hit Zaporizhzhia late Sunday, destroying a university building and hitting apartment blocks and a shopping mall (2 killed, 5 wounded, per Ukrainian officials). Russia launched 172 drones at 8 Ukrainian cities, framed by Moscow as retaliation for Ukraine's ~1,000-drone barrage on Moscow timed to the election weekend. Update (Sept 21 pm): Ukraine's MoD now says ~1,600 drones were launched nationwide overnight, ~450 toward Moscow (FT: Ukraine's largest-ever drone attack on Moscow); Russia's MoD claims 1,900+ drones downed plus guided bombs/cruise missiles/rockets -- each side's own claim. Zaporizhzhia casualty figures remain inconsistent across outlets (1-6 killed, 8-38 wounded) hours later, not resolved this run.
stories.score_note: Fresh casualty-producing escalation cycle in an active war.
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (wire + head-of-state statement); casualty figures are Ukrainian-official-sourced only

stories.headline: ICE officer shoots Venezuelan delivery driver in Austin; protests and a federal investigation follow
stories.one_line: DHS/ICE say the investigation is being led 'with assistance from the FBI'; Garcés Pérez remains in federal custody at Pearsall, described as stable. His attorney's allegations (bullet near spine, denied pain medication, made to sleep on floor) remain unconfirmed by DHS. Officer's identity and bodycam footage still not public. Rep. Casar demanding footage release; LULAC/NAACP/county commissioners held a joint Monday news conference.
stories.score_note: An ICE shooting of a civilian with no confirmed dashcam/bodycam release yet, drawing sustained local protest and federal-oversight demands.
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple on the shooting; Single-reliable-source on detention-conditions allegations

stories.headline: Zero-click 'Plugin4Shell' flaw hits AI coding agents; two of four tools still unpatched
stories.one_line: AIR Security disclosed a supply-chain flaw in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI's plugin/extension mechanisms that can defeat commit-pin verification and inherit a developer's local credentials. Anthropic (Claude Code 2.1.179) and OpenAI (Codex 0.146.0) have patched; Microsoft's Copilot and Google's Gemini CLI reportedly have not. No in-the-wild exploitation found by the researcher. Update (Sept 22): no material change -- GitHub Copilot remains unpatched; Google is reportedly discontinuing the consumer Gemini CLI product entirely rather than patching it (enterprise Gemini Code Assist unaffected). No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
stories.score_note: New AI-agent supply-chain risk category; follows last week's Cisco/Chrome/Patch Tuesday cluster.
stories.verification: Single primary source, corroborated only by trade-press syndication

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO marketing reportedly slips again, now to November
stories.one_line: Anthropic remains private ($965B post-money Series H, May 28; confidential S-1 reported ~June 1). This outlet's weekly EDGAR sweep (last run Sept 19) found no self-filing yet on public EDGAR. New Reuters/CNBC reporting says the IPO launch has shifted toward mid-October, conflicting with earlier September-target reports. Update (Sept 22): press reporting (Japan Times/Reuters, CNBC/Reuters, Fortune) has narrowed toward a mid-October marketing launch (not September), targeting a listing before the midterms at a reported ~$2T valuation; still no self-filing found on public EDGAR as of last Saturday's registry sweep. Update (Sept 23 am, single-reliable-source): Bloomberg reports the roadshow has shifted again, now to November, to fold in Q3 results; Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley reportedly preparing a listing near a $2T valuation and $100B raise backed by a $15B credit facility, Nvidia among reported interested strategic investors. Two unrelated issuers (Holtec Nuclear, Bamboo Insurance) postponed their own listings this week citing market conditions -- cited by Bloomberg as a caution flag ahead of Anthropic's debut.
stories.score_note: A closely watched AI-lab IPO; genuine timing disagreement between outlets, not just phrasing.
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple on the underlying confidential filing; timing disputed between outlets

stories.headline: PennDOT begins nightly I-79 lane restrictions near Bridgeville for six weeks of crack sealing
stories.one_line: PennDOT District 11 will run nightly (7pm-6am) lane restrictions in both directions on I-79 between the PA Turnpike/Airport/Morganza Rd interchange and the Route 50/Bridgeville interchange, weather permitting, through early November. Update (Sept 22): firm start date now set -- nightly restrictions begin overnight this Friday/Saturday, 7 PM-6 AM, through early November.
stories.score_note: Local Bridgeville/South Fayette beat -- affects nightly commuters for six weeks.

stories.headline: Paramount Skydance expects to close its $111B WBD merger within two weeks
stories.one_line: Consent decree terms (N.D. Cal.): $300M/year additional US film production (~$1.5B over 5 years); minimum release slate (30 films/year rising to 32) or risk penalties incl. possible forced Miramax divestiture; 5-year no-sale commitment on CA studio lots; separate cable-affiliate-fee negotiations; union-agreement and workforce-training commitments under an independent monitor. Ticker corrected to PSKY (post-merger; not pre-merger 'PARA') in the entity registry this run. $7M/day late fee to WBD shareholders past Sept 30 explains the settlement's timing. Update (Sept 23 am): CEO David Ellison told employees he expects closing within roughly two weeks; Paramount Skydance shares rose about 4% on the settlement, WBD little changed.
stories.score_note: Removes the last state-level legal obstacle to a $111B media merger already shareholder-approved.

stories.headline: Kremlin dismisses Trump's Ukraine territorial reversal as both sides strike each other's energy grids overnight
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple for the meeting and Truth Social post; Single-reliable-source for the 'Russia lost control of diesel' official characterization
stories.one_line: Meeting and Trump's UNGA address had not yet occurred as of this morning's publication. Overnight: Russia struck 4+ Ukrainian regions (200+ drones, missiles, 4 killed); Ukraine struck the Kuibyshev refinery in Samara. Follows Monday's Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia (172 drones, 8 cities, casualty counts diverge 1-2 dead across wires) which itself followed Ukraine's record 1,000+-drone barrage on Moscow during the Duma election. Update (Sept 22): the meeting took place; both sides agreed to pursue a truce limited to energy-infrastructure strikes, with technical talks to follow in Saudi Arabia. Trump's own Truth Social post afterward went well beyond that narrower agenda, saying Ukraine 'with the support of the European Union' can 'fight and WIN all of Ukraine back in its original form' -- a reversal of his prior position that a settlement would require ceding territory. No Russian response yet to either the meeting or the post. Update (Sept 23 am): Kremlin spokesman Peskov dismissed the territorial claim, saying Trump had simply absorbed 'Ukraine's perspective' and that Russia is 'a real bear,' not 'a paper bear.' Zelensky separately said Ukraine is 'ready' for a mutual energy-strike halt but no deal was reached for Kyiv to stand down unilaterally; overnight, Ukraine struck two Russian oil refineries and Russia hit an oil-and-gas facility in southern Ukraine officials call damaged beyond repair -- no ceasefire is yet operative on either side. No confirmation located of the Saudi Arabia technical talks reported to follow Monday's meeting.
stories.score_note: First Trump-Zelensky meeting since the new Russia sanctions law, opening with both sides escalating rather than de-escalating.

stories.headline: UN General Assembly week opens as Trump arrives in New York, meets Mayor Mamdani
stories.one_line: Trump arrived in New York today ahead of the UN General Assembly's 81st high-level week (opens tomorrow); met Mayor Zohran Mamdani at Gracie Mansion just before 4pm ET, their third in-person meeting, closed to press. No readout published as of this edition. Tomorrow: Trump addresses the assembly, with bilaterals reportedly including UK PM Andy Burnham (first in-person meeting) and Japan PM Sanae Takaichi (reportedly planning to raise China/Taiwan concerns pre-summit), plus the newly announced Zelensky meeting.
stories.score_note: Sets up a dense diplomatic week: UNGA address, multiple bilaterals, and the Trump-Xi summit Wed-Thu.

stories.headline: Transit advocates push riders to weigh in on PRT's bus-network redesign before Sept. 30
stories.one_line: Pittsburgh Regional Transit's proposed system-wide bus redesign (90 of 95 routes) drew fresh public pushback today; advocates urge riders to comment before the window closes Sept 30 and are pressing for a bolder version. Would boost frequency on core routes while cutting/eliminating service to some outlying communities (Ross, Monroeville, South Park reduced; parts of White Oak/Penn Hills could lose service entirely). Separate from the $94.1M/102-bus purchase the PRT board votes on Friday Sept 25.
stories.score_note: Local Pittsburgh/Allegheny beat -- affects South Hills-adjacent riders directly.

stories.headline: Two unresolved state Supreme Court rulings loom over PA legislature's Sept. 28 return
stories.one_line: PA's General Assembly returns Sept 28 with two unaddressed state Supreme Court rulings: the March 26 decision striking down mandatory life-without-parole for felony murder as unconstitutional (lawmakers already missed the court's deadline to write a replacement sentencing scheme -- up to 1,100+ affected in what could become the state's largest resentencing effort), and the June 15 ruling that 'skill game' terminals are illegal slot machines (State Police confirm enforcement/seizure begins Oct 14, absent legislative action -- affects South Hills bars, taverns, VFWs, convenience stores).
stories.score_note: Local Pennsylvania beat -- direct statewide and South Hills small-business impact.

stories.headline: AMD's trillion-dollar milestone holds -- Tuesday's dip was profit-taking, not a reversal
stories.one_line: AMD rose ~10% Monday to close $615.52, crossing $1T market cap for the first time (5-day rally ~24%), the 4th US chipmaker over $1T after Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron. Rally followed Meta's 'Muse' AI agent becoming Apple's #1 free app (~730K downloads in 5 days); Intel +~12%, Arm +~17%, Meta +11%+. Tuesday premarket: NVDA/AMD/INTC/MRVL all pulled back, coinciding with the 30-year Treasury yield hitting ~5.33% (highest since 2007) and fading US-Iran settlement hopes keeping oil elevated -- described as profit-taking, a likely contributor not a confirmed cause. Update (Sept 23 am): confirmed as profit-taking, not a reversal -- AMD closed Tuesday at $623.77, above Monday's close, holding the $1T milestone.
stories.score_note: A chipmaker crossing $1T market cap and giving back a chunk of the move within 24 hours is a genuine, fast-moving market story.

stories.headline: Federal judge rules EPA unlawfully terminated the $7B Solar for All grant program
stories.one_line: A federal judge ruled Monday the EPA's termination of Solar for All (an IRA-era program funding solar installation for disadvantaged communities) was unlawful, finding Congress clearly intended EPA to keep administering already-obligated grants. Latest in a string of court losses for the administration this month.
stories.score_note: A concrete legal check on a federal funding termination, with a clear practical effect on already-obligated grants.

stories.headline: FDA approves first-ever treatment for Alexander disease
stories.one_line: FDA approved zilganersen (Zanvastro), from Ionis Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: IONS), as the first-ever treatment for Alexander disease, an ultra-rare fatal neurological condition. Phase III showed statistically significant gait-speed stabilization; Ionis's first independently commercialized neurology launch, expected available in coming weeks.
stories.score_note: A genuine first-in-class approval for a disease with no prior treatment option.
